title: NASA Detects Water Vapor in Exoplanet Atmosphere; CRISPR Gene Editing Cures Sickle Cell Disease in Landmark Trial; Quantum Computer Breaks Error Correction Threshold

articles.headline: NASA's Webb Telescope Detects Water Vapor Signal in Exoplanet Atmosphere
articles.summary: Latest observations from the James Webb Space Telescope reveal significant water vapor signals in the atmosphere of exoplanet K2-18b, located 120 light-years from Earth. This discovery provides compelling evidence that the planet may host liquid water oceans. The research team described this as the clearest water vapor signature ever detected on a habitable-zone exoplanet, expanding our understanding of exoplanet atmospheric composition and offering new clues in the search for extraterrestrial life.

sources.title: NASA Webb Reveals New Details in Exoplanet Atmosphere

articles.headline: CRISPR Gene Editing Achieves Breakthrough Success in Sickle Cell Disease Treatment
articles.summary: A multi-center clinical trial shows that sickle cell disease patients treated with CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing achieved complete symptom remission after 18 months of follow-up. This marks the first time the technology has demonstrated sustained efficacy in a randomized controlled trial. Researchers edited patients' own hematopoietic stem cells to produce healthy hemoglobin. While long-term safety monitoring continues, the results are considered a milestone in gene therapy.

articles.headline: Quantum Computer Breaks Error Correction Threshold for the First Time
articles.summary: Google Quantum AI announced its next-generation quantum processor has surpassed the theoretical error correction threshold for the first time. This means adding more error-correcting qubits reduces the system's logical error rate — a necessary condition for practical quantum computing. The processor uses 105 physical qubits to achieve a lower error rate than a previous 72-qubit system, validating the scalability of the surface code error correction scheme.
